mission: FLI works to reduce extreme risks from transformative technologies, above all advanced AI, and also biotechnology and nuclear weapons. It does policy advocacy in the US, EU and UN, runs public communication campaigns, funds research through grants, and publishes the AI Safety Index grading frontier AI companies. It is best known for the 2017 Asilomar AI Principles and the 2023 open letter calling for a pause on giant AI experiments.

key_work.title: FLI AI Safety Index (Summer 2026 edition)
key_work.plain_summary: An independent scorecard that grades the leading AI companies on their safety practices, risk management and transparency.

key_work.title: The Pro-Human AI Declaration
key_work.plain_summary: A broad, cross-partisan declaration calling for AI that serves people rather than replaces them, launched with an unusual coalition of signatories.

key_work.title: Statement on Superintelligence
key_work.plain_summary: A public call, signed by scientists, public figures and others, to prohibit developing superintelligence until there is broad scientific consensus it can be done safely and strong public buy-in.

key_work.title: Keep the Future Human (Anthony Aguirre essay)
key_work.plain_summary: Argues we should close the 'gates' to autonomous general AI and instead build powerful but controllable AI tools.

key_work.title: Pause Giant AI Experiments: An Open Letter
key_work.plain_summary: The widely-signed March 2023 letter asking AI labs to pause training systems more powerful than GPT-4 for at least six months.

key_work.title: Asilomar AI Principles
key_work.plain_summary: 23 principles for beneficial AI agreed at FLI's 2017 Asilomar conference — one of the first widely endorsed AI governance frameworks.

warnings.text: The race to build superintelligence risks humanity losing control of its future.
AI companies' safety practices lag far behind their capabilities (per the AI Safety Index).
AI is being built to replace people rather than empower them.
Recursive self-improvement by AI systems could quickly escape human oversight.

recommendations.text: Prohibit superintelligence until there is scientific consensus it is safe and controllable, and public buy-in.
Build controllable 'tool AI' instead of autonomous general agents.
Binding safety standards and independent oversight for frontier AI companies.
Pressure AI companies to immediately limit the use of recursive self-improvement.
